headline: A Goldman Sachs executive says new finance hires will manage AI agents from their first day at work.
score_reason: Pool 6; event 8 Oct 2026, so no stale lowering; remarks from one panel, so no raise.
importance_line: The career ladder for new finance hires may be reshaped, which affects graduates and junior bankers first and then middle managers, and the doubt is that these are remarks on a conference panel rather than a stated bank plan.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by The Straits Times, that Kevin Sneader, who leads Goldman Sachs' business in Asia-Pacific outside Japan, told the Milken Institute Asia Summit in Singapore on 8 Oct 2026 that new hires now oversee AI agents from their first day. He said nobody quite knows what will happen to middle managers, and Chia Der Jiun, managing director of the Monetary Authority of Singapore, said banks will need fewer fresh graduates for analysis and preparation work.
notes: Bloomberg original blocked (HTTP 403 captcha); text read on The Straits Times copy that carries the Bloomberg tag. Source is Bloomberg. Remarks are from a panel, not a bank policy.
